A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and are readable throughout. However, v1 includes Appendices A–F, whereas v3 ends after its references while retaining appendix cross-references. Supplementary-content judgments below concern its observable absence from the supplied v3.pdf, not any unprovided supplement.

before.justification: v1 reports original reading-recognition experiments, generalization tests, ablations, and reading-type classification, with additional experiments in Appendices D–F.

after.justification: v3 retains original Seattle, Columbus, and EGTEA experiments, modality ablations, real-time detection results, and reading-type classification.

M1.justification: The convolutional modality encoders, transformer fusion, modality dropout, inputs, and inference transformations remain unchanged. Rotation augmentation was already documented in v1 Section 5.2; gaze-scaling personalization in v3 Section 6.3 condenses v1 Appendix F.2 rather than introducing a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain the Seattle and Columbus subsets, EGTEA, multilingual reading, alternating sequences, and reading-mode/medium classification. Missing supplementary breakdowns do not establish removal of the underlying datasets, populations, or scenarios, which remain represented in the retained evaluations.

E2.justification: v3 omits the external-method comparisons reported in v1 Appendix E: Llama-3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct, two-stream I3D, and gaze-only GRU/RNN, CNN, and MLP alternatives. These were actually evaluated in v1; the retained modality comparisons do not replace them.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation scope loses v1's supplementary Columbus AUC and threshold-tuned accuracy/F1 metrics, full-frame versus cropped/blank-image VLM tests, EGTEA baseline evaluation designs, and RGB-assisted medium-classification configuration. The shared main-text splits, training budget, metrics, and default inputs remain unchanged; no rerun is established.

E4.justification: v3 omits Appendix D's Columbus breakdowns by content and medium, expanded multilingual modality tests, mirror-setup evaluation, and detailed success/failure cases, including misleading RGB crops and reading signs while walking. Main-text modality, input, model-size, noise, and generalization analyses remain.

E5.justification: The matched experiments retain the same reporting practice, with no added or revised repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The omitted supplementary result tables likewise report point estimates.

E6.justification: Main results match, including 86.9% Seattle accuracy and 88.8 Columbus F1 for the combined model. Extensive supplementary results disappear, including I3D's EGTEA accuracy/F1 of 88.8/65.8 in v1 Table 13 and mirror-setup results in Table 12. v3 adds an estimated runtime of at least four hours on Aria Gen 2, not a same-setting recognition-performance gain.

T1.justification: Section 4 retains the same task definition and mathematical formulation of modality encoding and transformer prediction. Neither version presents additional theorems, proofs, or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: an in-the-wild reading-recognition task and dataset, complementary sensing modalities, a lightweight flexible baseline, and extensions to reading understanding.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive discussion of gaze privacy, bystander surveillance, governance, and practical deployment. It omits most supplementary explanations of modality failures and limitations from Appendices D–F. Reading-speed personalization is retained in condensed form, so that interpretation is not new.

D1.justification: v3 loses detailed collection instructions, annotation and segmentation procedures, metadata examples, participant information, baseline prompts, hyperparameters, and comparative inference timings from the appendices. It adds a project-page link, venue-privacy clarification, and Aria Gen 2 deployment information. Code, models, and data are still described as forthcoming.

R1.justification: The main related-work positioning remains essentially unchanged. With Appendix E absent, v3 drops references to Carreira and Zisserman's I3D work, Grattafiori et al.'s Llama work, and Min and Corso's gaze-informed activity recognition, alongside the supplementary comparison discussion.

P1.justification: The document loses the entire A–F supplementary narrative and subsection structure, including separate comparison and limitations discussions. v3 adds a Broader Impact section and incorporates condensed personalization discussion into Section 6.3. Most matched main-text prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The supplied v3 omits supplementary Figures 9–34 and Tables 7–14, including dataset distributions, annotation examples, diagnostic plots, and baseline comparisons. Main Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–6 remain with layout relocation and small refinements, such as adding seconds to the latency column.

improvement.justification: As supplied, v3 substantially weakens reproducibility and evidential support by losing detailed collection/annotation protocols, external-method comparisons, and extensive diagnostic analyses from v1's appendices. The new privacy/governance discussion, project link, and deployment estimate are useful, but do not compensate for those losses. Retained appendix cross-references also leave important supporting material inaccessible within v3.pdf.
